service.name: Live music for a holiday party at home
service.serviceType: A Christmas party band, a Christmas jazz duo or trio, live band karaoke or a DJ for holiday parties at home, Thanksgiving week dinners and New Year's Eve at a house
service.description: Live music for a holiday party at home across Denver and the Front Range: a Christmas jazz duo or trio playing the season and the standards at 65 to 72 dBA, a singer with a guitar, a party band for the floor, live band karaoke for a big main floor, and a DJ through the same sound system on the same contract, with sound support sized to the house and one personal contact for the night.

faqs.q: Can we book a band for a Christmas party at home?
faqs.a: Yes. A house books one guitarist or a singer with a guitar for an open house or a dinner, the Christmas jazz duo or trio for drinks and dinner, a party band for the part of the night when the furniture moves, and a DJ on its own or after the band. It's one contract with one personal contact, booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

faqs.q: Do you play Christmas music, or just the standards?
faqs.a: Both, and the balance is yours. The Christmas jazz trio draws on the Vince Guaraldi record from the Charlie Brown special, the standards that are Christmas songs, and the standards that aren't, threaded through so a three-hour party doesn't hear the same carols twice.

faqs.q: How loud is it in a house?
faqs.a: At dinner, about the level of the conversation around it, so nobody at the table raises their voice. A party band turns up once the furniture moves, and the loud part of a winter party is indoors anyway, which makes December the easy month for the neighbors. If your building or HOA has quiet hours in writing, give them to us at contract.

faqs.q: How much space does the band need in a house?
faqs.a: A solo or a DJ takes about 6 by 4 feet, a duo 8 by 6, a trio 12 by 8 and a quartet 14 by 10. Each wants one dedicated circuit that the oven and the coffee makers aren't on (the quartet and the karaoke four-piece want two). Setup runs 45 minutes for a solo or a DJ and an hour for a duo or a trio. The tree usually stands in the corner the band would take, so tell us which corner is ours, and tell us about the driveway or the alley for unloading.

faqs.q: Is a dinner for twelve big enough for live music?
faqs.a: Yes. A dinner for twelve books one guitarist or a singer with a guitar in a corner, and an open house books a duo that works whether twelve or sixty people are in the house at the time.
